subject: Confirming commitment: we do not incorporate customer data into model training
messages:
From: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@paylend.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya@paylend.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Quick confirmation: Is customer data used for model training?

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we dig into the security questionnaire (SOC2 + data processing), Legal flagged the claim in your docs that Redwood does not incorporate customer prompt/response content into internal model training. Before we include that language in our procurement packet we need a couple of clarifications: 

- Does this cover ephemeral logs, debug snapshots, and any telemetry used for performance tuning?
- Are there any retention exceptions (backups, cold archives, regulatory holds) where data might persist beyond the normal TTL?
- What is your purge process for customer-requested erasure — does it remove replicas and backups, and what timelines apply?

Can you point us to a short attestation we can attach to the SOW and a contact for a technical walkthrough?

Best,
Evan
Senior Director, Security & Compliance
PayLend

Attachment: none

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@paylend.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya@paylend.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 10:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Quick confirmation: Is customer data used for model training?

Hi Evan —

Appreciate the clear list of asks. Short answer: Redwood does not use customer prompts, responses, or uploaded content to train or continually update our public models. We maintain a formal attestation for customers that states this explicitly — I attached the customer-facing attestation for quick review. 

To address each bullet:
- Ephemeral logs & debug snapshots: we treat customer content in runtime logs as operational telemetry. By default we do not surface those datasets to model training pipelines. Some internal telemetry (metrics, anonymized latencies) are used for service quality improvements, but not as training corpora.
- Retention exceptions: backups and cold archives are retained according to the retention matrix (attached). We do have a standard backup retention window (30 days for hot snapshots, 90 days for cold archives) unless longer retention is contractually required or legally compelled. Those backups are excluded from training processes.
- Purge process: Customer erasure requests trigger a staged purge: mark-for-delete -> remove from hot-tier -> schedule snapshot purge. We aim to remove primary copies within 72 hours and purge backups within the applicable retention window unless there is an active legal hold. Rishi is cc'd for technical specifics on snapshot lifecycle.

If you want, we can provide a short contract addendum (DocuSign) and a technical runbook for filing with your security team.

Cheers,
Marissa
Enterprise Lead, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

--
Attachments: redwood-nontraining-attestation.pdf

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@paylend.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya@paylend.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 14:18:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Quick confirmation: Is customer data used for model training?

Evan —

Adding a bit more color from an ops perspective so your engineers have concrete artifacts to review. Key points: 

1) Training pipelines: strictly separated. There are no automated connectors that push customer data (prompts/responses) into model training corpora. Model training runs are executed from curated datasets (internal benchmarks and open datasets) on an isolated infra account.

2) Snapshots & backups: we take continuous KV-cache and model-serving state snapshots for fast failover. Hot-tier snapshots (short-term) live for 30 days by default; archived snapshots for disaster recovery are kept for up to 90 days unless contracted otherwise. All snapshots are encrypted at rest with customer-specific keys for Redwood Private customers; hosted customers use account-scoped encryption keys.

3) Purge behavior: when a customer requests erasure, we: 
  - create a pending-erase marker,
  - remove operational copies from active stores within 72 hours,
  - schedule snapshot deletion jobs (subject to the retention window) — snapshot purge jobs run weekly and may take an additional 7–14 days to fully evict all archived shards.

4) Legal holds: any subpoena or compliance hold will suspend automated purge jobs for the duration of the hold; we will notify the customer with the hold reference.

If PayLend needs shortened snapshot purge SLA, we can include a special clause in the SOW (e.g., 7-day snapshot purge for an additional commitment).

-rishi
Director, Production Engineering
Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa + Rishi — that helps a lot. A couple of quick follow-ups from Legal/InfoSec:

- For the purge timeline, we need confirmation in writing that snapshot purge will be attempted within 14 days of an erase request (including archive eviction), unless a legal hold is active.

If you can provide the updated attestation and a DocuSign addendum, we can move this into procurement.

Regards,
Evan
